Soil health cards tell each farmer exactly which nutrients the field needs.

Most people think saving money means giving up everything they enjoy. It does not.
It starts with knowing where your money goes.
For one month, write down every rupee you spend: rent, groceries, the bus fare, the late-night snack.
At the end of the month, sort
it into three
groups: needs, wants and savings.
You will be surprised how much slips away on small things nobody remembers buying. Next, pay yourself first.
On payday, move a fixed amount into a separate savings account before you spend anything else.
Even five percent of your salary adds up.
Then build an emergency fund that covers three months of expenses, so a broken phone or a hospital bill does not push you into debt.
Cook at home a few more nights each week, cancel the subscriptions you forgot about, and compare prices before every big purchase.
Small habits, repeated every day, turn into real security.
Start this month, and in a year you will not recognise your bank balance.
